title: Spinach & Pepper Egg Muffins
headnote: Grab-and-go egg cups you can bake once and reheat all week. Swap in whatever vegetables are in the fridge.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
Whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Stir in the spinach, bell pepper, onion and cheddar.
Divide the mixture among the muffin cups and bake for 20 minutes, until set.
Cool slightly. Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 4 days.

title: Peanut Butter Waffles with Banana
headnote: Crisp, nutty waffles with a soft middle. The dry ingredients can be whisked together ahead of time.
steps: Heat a waffle iron.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt in a large bowl.
Whisk the eggs, milk, peanut butter and melted butter in a second bowl, then fold into the dry ingredients until just combined.
Cook in the hot waffle iron until golden and crisp.
Top with the sliced banana.

title: Berry Overnight Oats
headnote: Four breakfasts in one bowl: stir, portion, chill. They keep for up to four days.
steps: Stir the oats, milk, yogurt, chia seeds, honey and vanilla together in a large bowl.
Divide the mixture among 4 containers.
Refrigerate overnight.
Top with the berries just before eating.

title: Veggie Breakfast Burritos
headnote: Eggs, black beans and peppers rolled up tight. Wrap them individually and reheat from the fridge or freezer.
ingredients: 1 (15-oz) can black beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Warm the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the bell pepper and onion until soft, about 6 minutes.
Add the beans and cumin and cook 2 minutes more.
Beat the eggs with the salt, pour into the skillet and stir gently until just set.
Divide the filling among the tortillas, top with the cheddar and salsa, and roll up tightly.
Wrap each burrito in foil and refrigerate for up to 4 days, or freeze for up to 2 months.

title: Sweet Potato & Black Bean Hash with Eggs
headnote: A one-skillet hash that works for breakfast or dinner. The eggs cook right on top.
ingredients: 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
1 (15-oz) can black beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook the sweet potatoes for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned.
Add the onion, bell pepper, paprika and salt and cook 6 minutes more.
Stir in the beans. Make four wells, crack an egg into each, cover and cook 4 minutes.
Top with the cilantro.

title: Chickpea Salad Sandwiches
headnote: Crunchy, lemony and ready in fifteen minutes. The salad keeps for three days, so make a double batch.
steps: Mash the chickpeas roughly with a fork in a large bowl.
Stir in the yogurt, celery, red onion, lemon juice, mustard, salt and pepper.
Layer the chickpea salad and spinach between slices of bread.

title: Caprese Pasta Salad
headnote: Tomatoes, mozzarella and basil tossed with pasta. It tastes better after a night in the fridge.
steps: Cook the pasta in salted boiling water until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water.
Whisk the olive oil, balsamic vinegar, salt and pepper into a dressing.
Toss the pasta with the dressing, tomatoes, mozzarella and torn basil.
Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving.

title: Lentil Vegetable Soup
headnote: A sturdy, plant-based soup that only gets better on day two. A squeeze of lemon at the end wakes it up.
steps: Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots and celery until soft, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, tomatoes, broth and salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 30 minutes, until the lentils are tender.
Stir in the spinach and lemon juice. Season to taste.

title: Hearty Vegetable Soup
headnote: A big pot of vegetables, white beans and greens. It freezes beautifully, so portion what you won't eat this week.
ingredients: 1 (15-oz) can white beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots and celery until soft, about 10 minutes.
Add the garlic, tomatoes and broth. Simmer for 25 minutes, crushing the tomatoes with a spoon.
Stir in the white beans and spinach and cook until the spinach wilts. Season to taste.

title: Quinoa Black Bean Bowls
headnote: Fluffy quinoa, beans, corn and a bright lime dressing. Pack it cold for lunch.
ingredients: 1 (15-oz) can black beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Cook the quinoa in 2 cups of water until tender and the water is absorbed, about 15 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Whisk the lime juice, olive oil, cumin and salt into a dressing.
Toss the quinoa, beans, corn, bell pepper, red onion and cilantro with the dressing.
Serve topped with sliced avocado.
